integrity: The standard p>=1 theorem is proved directly from the exact cone-volume weights of a translated regular polygon and strict convexity of a one-variable kernel. The log endpoint is computed from the equal cone-volume atoms. A standalone checker reconstructs polygon supports and numerically stress-tests the formulas; no finite computation is used as an infinite proof. The first_public_date records the exact verified public author-upload date of the inspected full text; bibliographic sources also label the work as 2017/2018 but did not expose an earlier exact public day in the inspected evidence.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is specific to regular planar polygons. The ordinary Minkowski endpoint is elementary and may be recorded in older terminology. The originality assessment concerns the combined log/standard-p spectrum and critical-point structure. The 0<p<1 extension is explicitly qualified because the accessible Section 4 displayed definition is textually ambiguous while its proof uses the normalized p-mixed volume.
title: Collapse of log and p-Minkowski asymmetry on regular polygons
